hmpo-passport#eligibility.criteria.0.rationale: partly supported: The text implies citizens of a British overseas territory can apply, but it never lists which categories count as British national, so British citizens and the other unspecified categories are not set out.

hmcts-divorce#eligibility.criteria.1.rationale: partly supported: The six-month residence ground applies only to the applicant, who must also be domiciled there, and requires six months immediately before the application, not 6 of the last 12 months; otherwise habitual residence needs one year or applies to the respondent, both parties, or either party in a joint application.

hmcts-gender-recognition#eligibility.cri.rationale: not stated: The listed requirements (age 18+, UK diagnosis, 2 years living in affirmed gender, intention to continue) say nothing about nationality or permanent residence; only the separate no-diagnosis route requires that you currently live in the UK.

hmcts-legal-aid#eligibility.criteria.1.rationale: partly supported: A prospects of success criterion (reg. 43) applies to full representation, but the regulations do not apply it to other forms of legal aid such as legal help.

la-blue-badge#eligibility.criteria.0.rationale: partly supported: The text treats non-visible (hidden) conditions as a route to eligibility, with criteria such as struggling severely to plan or follow a journey, but it does not use a 'very considerable difficulty' threshold for hidden conditions.

ch-close-company#eligibility.exclusions..rationale: not stated: The text does not mention legal proceedings as a bar to closing a company.

dwp-voluntary-ni-contributions#eligibili.rationale: partly supported: The text excludes people with no gaps in their record, not people already entitled to the full State Pension; it only says voluntary contributions do not always increase the State Pension.

insolvency-bankruptcy#eligibility.exclus.rationale: partly supported: The Act bars an order where a bankruptcy order already covers the debts in the application, but does not say that being already bankrupt excludes the person outright.

la-blue-badge#eligibility.autoQualifiers.rationale: partly supported: The text grants automatic eligibility for PIP mobility based on a score of 8 or more points for moving around, or 10 points under descriptor E, and asks for proof of the PIP award, but it never mentions the enhanced rate.

la-disabled-facilities-grant#agentIntera.rationale: not stated: None of the sources mention applying in person; they describe applying through the council online, by phone or by letter, and an occupational therapist visit as part of assessment.

dvla-cancel-licence#eligibility.evidence.rationale: not stated: The source never mentions a D27 form; it says to write a letter to DVLA and include the person's driving licence.

dwp-inherited-state-pension#eligibility..rationale: partly supported: The text asks for the date of the most recent marriage or civil partnership when claiming, but never mentions providing a marriage or civil partnership certificate.

la-school-place#eligibility.evidenceRequ.rationale: partly supported: Only Bromley council's admissions page requires the child's birth certificate (long form only); the GOV.UK page does not say it is needed by councils generally.

sss-best-start-foods#eligibility.evidenc.rationale: not stated: The text says when you can apply during pregnancy but does not say any proof of pregnancy is required. not stated: The text sets age limits for the child but does not say any proof of the child's age is required.

la-electoral-roll#desc.rationale: partly supported: The text says you give both addresses on one register to vote form and are then removed from the old address automatically, not that you update at both addresses separately.

nhs-continuing-healthcare#desc.rationale: not stated: The sources describe health and social care but do not mention specialist support.
